scenarios.name: Founder interview: intro, basics, flowchart, sequence diagram

checks.them: Let's do something visual. Can you draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen in our app?

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: Local database is the single source of truth; the screen only reads from it
card.heard: draw a flowchart, send tap to streamed reply on screen
card.say: Sure. I'll draw the whole path in one picture. The user taps send, and the app saves the message in the local database first. Then it sends it to the backend, and the backend calls the AI. The reply comes back as a stream, and the app shows each piece as it arrives.
card.type: draw@chat send to streamed reply: flowchart TD ⏎ A[User taps send] --> B[Save message to local DB] ⏎ B --> C[Send request to backend] ⏎ C --> D[Backend calls AI] ⏎ D --> E[Reply streams back] ⏎ E --> F[Save each piece to local DB] ⏎ F --> G[Screen shows reply]
card.then: Next I'd add the failure path: what happens when the stream breaks.

checks.them: What happens in that flow if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: Local database is the single source of truth; the screen only reads from it
card.constraints: ["If the network drops halfway through the reply, the app must handle it and show it in the diagram"]
card.heard: what happens if the network drops mid-reply, add it to the diagram
card.say: When the stream breaks, the app keeps the chunks it already saved. It marks the message as incomplete in the database, so the screen shows a clear "not finished" state. Then it reconnects and asks the server for the rest, using the last chunk it has. The server would need to resend from that point, and the app ignores any chunk it already saved.
card.type: draw@chat-stream diagram: flowchart TD ⏎     A[Stream breaks] --> B[Mark message incomplete in DB] ⏎     B --> C[Reconnect with last chunk id] ⏎     C --> D[Server resends from that point] ⏎     D --> E[App saves new chunks, skips duplicates] ⏎     E --> F[Screen shows reply complete]
card.then: Next I'd cover what the user sees while it's reconnecting.

checks.them: Good. Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it.

card.problem: Draw a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it
card.heard: new request — sequence diagram of login with token refresh
card.say: Okay, I'll draw the login flow as a sequence diagram. The app sends the username and password to the backend. The backend checks them and returns an access token and a refresh token. The app saves both tokens, and the screen moves to the home page.
card.type: draw@login sequence: sequenceDiagram ⏎     participant App ⏎     participant Server ⏎     App->>Server: POST /login (username, password) ⏎     Server-->>App: access token + refresh token ⏎     App->>App: save tokens ⏎     App->>Server: GET /home (access token) ⏎     Server-->>App: home data
card.then: Next, the expired-token part: the server rejects the call, and the app refreshes the token.
